children.objective: Isolate the benefit of CPU worksharing across stencil rows or planes, using the run-time threads argument as the thread budget. Consider a persistent OpenMP parallel region around the six steps to avoid repeated team-startup overhead, while retaining the required global synchronization between steps and even/odd buffer semantics. Include initialization only if measurements justify it. Validate and compare repeated results at both sizes and both thread budgets; do not combine this track with temporal fusion or a new SIMD kernel.
children.subject: OpenMP worksharing and persistent stencil-step region

children.objective: Using the existing compiler configuration, first determine whether GCC already vectorizes the contiguous-x loop, then compare compiler-directed vectorization with an explicit SIMD implementation if appropriate. Handle all interior bounds and tails for every valid size, preserve results within tolerance, and do not change compiler options or restructure threading or timesteps. Compare correctness and repeated timings at every official size/thread combination.
children.subject: GCC SIMD effectiveness in the single-step x kernel

children.objective: Investigate spatial tiling across the six timesteps to reuse intermediate values and reduce full-volume traffic. Account for radius-three dependencies at each step, alternating buffers, and the initialized values of fixed boundary regions. The complete output must still contain both specified buffers with the correct final interior values and preserved boundaries; scratch-allocation cost is timed. Support every valid input size and compare correctness and repeated timings at every official size/thread combination.
children.subject: Temporal blocking with complete two-buffer output preservation

decision.rationale: Je vais examiner le code mesuré de Gm1 avant de choisir une intégration; ses 0,00452 s et la mesure plus lente de Gm2 motivent de préserver ce candidat de référence.
Examiner la variante T2 `omp simd` mesurée la plus rapide pour déterminer si son ajout de `restrict` constitue une modification compatible et ciblée de Gm1.

Tester l’ajout ciblé des qualificateurs `__restrict__` de cacd aux pointeurs du noyau Gm1, sans remplacer son équipe OpenMP persistante, son partage par plans z, ses barrières ni son chemin sériel. Gm1 est correct à 0,00452 s; cacd est correct à 0,00765 s en standalone. L’évaluateur doit mesurer si les annotations aident la combinaison. Écarter si la correction échoue ou si le temps n’améliore pas Gm1.

La première intégration `__restrict__` est correcte mais n’a pas dépassé Gm1. Examiner l’alternative mesurée de partage statique sur lignes aplaties (z,y) avant de décider si elle mérite une intégration distincte au noyau SIMD de Gm1.

La première intégration avec `__restrict__` est correcte mais légèrement plus lente que Gm1 (0,004574 contre 0,004521 s); je ne conserve pas ces annotations. Tester à la place le partage par lignes aplaties (z,y) de 9e tout en gardant le SIMD x de Gm1, son chemin sériel et les barrières. Le programme 9e est correct, mais son temps standalone (0,02073 s contre 0,02048 s pour le partage par plans) ne prouve aucun avantage; cette mesure teste leur interaction, sans présumer d’un gain.

Gm1 reste le meilleur programme correct mesuré à 0,004521 s. Les deux intégrations essayées étaient correctes, mais plus lentes : 0,004574 s avec __restrict__ et 0,004671 s avec le partage par lignes aplaties. Je ne retiens donc pas ces variantes; le contrôleur peut sélectionner le meilleur programme vérifié.

children.objective: Compare a persistent OpenMP team with per-step parallel regions, and include a serial fast path where appropriate, while honoring the threads budget. Workshare independent interior rows or slabs; retain the required barrier between time steps and correct buffer swaps. Preserve initialization and boundaries for arbitrary valid n. Measure correctness and native wall-clock time at both thread budgets, including one-thread overhead and the four-thread result.
children.subject: Thread-budgeted OpenMP parallelism across independent stencil points

children.objective: Isolate the per-core x-direction SIMD kernel: contrast compiler-autovectorized code with explicit intrinsics where useful, without adding an independent OpenMP work-sharing scheme or temporal blocking. The x start and shifted neighbor addresses need not be aligned, so do not assume alignment beyond the input contract. Handle tails and arbitrary valid n, preserve the numerical tolerance, and retain a correct implementation under the supplied thread budget. Compare correctness and timing; do not assume wider vectors or reassociation are faster or sufficiently accurate.
children.subject: Per-core SIMD/vectorization of the row-major stencil kernel

children.objective: Focus on reuse across the six time steps: compare an unfused spatially tiled control with one or more correctly fused temporal depths, so any fusion benefit is distinguishable from spatial tiling alone. Account for the radius-3 dependency halo at each fused step, the fixed active interior and unchanged inactive cells, buffer parity, arbitrary dimensions and tails, full output initialization, and scratch-allocation cost. Do not spend the objective on a separate SIMD kernel; structure a successful tile body for later combination. Measure correctness and native wall-clock time under the official protocol, and keep any useful slower intermediate as a potential integration component.
children.subject: Temporal fusion and working-set reuse across stencil steps
